chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Writing "Love, Love, Love" with Sid Wyche; BMI pen names
summary: With Wyche he wrote his first rock-and-roll hit, publishing under pseudonyms Thomas Bear and William Gray for BMI.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. But I wanna tell you about this area, because (inaudible) -- when you come out off the road -- after you've been on the road for a couple of years, you don't feel like (inaudible). I didn't wanna come in and start taking somebody else's job -- somebody working at, say, the Baby Grand and somebody working out -- It wasn't no place around New York that interested me to work, you know, coming out of the big band. So I just started gigging and just recording and writing. So what happened was, somebody had called us ---called me up and asked me could I get them some music for this date -- this rock and roll date. And Sid Wyche was another rock and roll writer. So I started writing with him. Now you see, here's a fella can write lyrics, but he need somebody to help him with the
